```console
"""Fig. 4: ratio the source-only variance formula predicts vs the ratio observed, one point per benchmark x split.
usage: python3 figures/scripts/fig4_ceiling.py CODE_DIR OUT_PDF
Sources: results/ceiling.csv (q_* = fraction of the Bernoulli variance of the unsampled items explained by the predictor,
uniform design, n = 100), results/per_bench.csv (observed ratio of common.OURS at n = 100).
Predicted ratio = sqrt(1 - q): the RMSE ratio a difference estimator reaches if its residual variance is (1-q) times
that of the constant predictor (finite-population factor identical in both). Left: q of the source-only predictor
(source item means, no target answers); right: q of the 2D IRT predictor that uses the target's n answers."""
import sys
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0, __file__.rsplit("/", 1)[0])
import style, common

style.apply()
R = common.Results(sys.argv[1])
ce = R.csv("ceiling.csv"); pb = R.csv("per_bench.csv")
ce = ce[ce.n == 100]
ob = pb[(pb.method == common.OURS) & (pb.n == 100)][["bench", "split", "ratio", "thin", "N"]]
d = ce.merge(ob, on=["bench", "split"])
MK = {"interp": "o", "extrap": "s", "lineage": "^", "extrap10": "d", "extrap50": "v"}
LAB = dict(common.SPLIT_LABEL, extrap10="extrap., top 10%", extrap50="extrap., top 50%", lineage="lineage-held-out")
SPL = ["interp", "extrap", "lineage", "extrap10", "extrap50"]
W, H = style.TEXT_WIDTH_IN, 2.9
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(W, H), sharey=True)
col = style.CLASS_STYLE["design-based"]["color"]
for ax, (q, ttl) in zip(axs, [("q_p", "predictor: source item means"), ("q_irt", "predictor: 2D IRT, target's $n$ answers")]):
    xs = np.sqrt(np.clip(1 - d[q], 0, None))
    for sp in SPL:
        s = d.split == sp
        for thin in (False, True):
            t = s & (d.thin == thin)
            if not t.any():
                continue
            c = col if sp in ("interp", "extrap", "lineage") else "#D55E00"
            ax.scatter(xs[t], d.ratio[t], marker=MK[sp], s=14, lw=0.8, facecolors="none" if thin else c,
                       edgecolors="0.55" if thin else c, label=None if thin else LAB[sp])
    lo, hi = max(0.0, 0.9 * float(min(xs.min(), d.ratio.min()))), max(1.05, float(max(xs.max(), d.ratio.max())) * 1.05)
    ax.plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], color="0.5", lw=0.6)
    ax.text(0.78 * hi, 0.78 * hi, "observed = prediction", rotation=45, rotation_mode="anchor", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=style.MIN_FONT_PT, color="0.4")
    ax.axhline(1, color="0.7", lw=0.5, ls=":"); ax.axvline(1, color="0.7", lw=0.5, ls=":")
    ax.set_xlim(lo, hi); ax.set_ylim(lo, hi); ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_title(ttl, loc="left"); ax.set_xlabel("SRS-residual prediction, √(1 − q)")
axs[0].set_ylabel("observed RMSE ratio, " + common.label(common.OURS).replace("×", r"$\times$"))
h, l = axs[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
seen = dict(zip(l, h))
seen["thin benchmark (hollow)"] = plt.Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", mfc="none", mec="0.55", mew=0.8, ms=4)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.085, right=0.985, top=0.77, bottom=0.17, wspace=0.12)
fig.legend(seen.values(), seen.keys(), loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.0), ncol=3, columnspacing=1.2, handletextpad=0.1, borderaxespad=0.1)
plt.rcParams["savefig.bbox"] = "standard"; fig.savefig(sys.argv[2])
8:TEXT_WIDTH_IN = 5.5   # NeurIPS text width
```

shown.message:
I found a type-size problem in Fig. 4 and fixed it on my `main` (f204e22). It reaches the paper once `paper-repo` syncs `figures/`, which I asked for in `paper-repo`#12.

- **Cause:** `paper-repo` placed Fig. 4 at 0.9 of the text width in cf2ce74. That scaled the 7 pt type down to 6.3 pt, under the venue's 7 pt minimum.
- **Fix:** I redrew Fig. 4 at 356.4 pt wide, which is 0.9 of the text width. The panels keep their size and the height stays 209 pt. At 0.9 of the text width it is shown 1:1, so the type stays 7 pt. I shortened the two panel titles so they fit, and noted the width in `figures/README.md`.
- **Check:** I viewed the new PDF and the titles and legend are not clipped. I did not check page count.
- **Fall-back rate:** `experiment-repo` confirmed that Table 10's n = 100 figures are correct (interpolation 4.5–6.0%, lineage 4.5–6.1%). The 21–22% was the 2% setting that had been attached to n = 100 by mistake. I told `paper-repo` in #12 not to quote it for n = 100.

`paper-repo` had already closed `figtab-repo`#8. `experiment-repo`#2 stays open for the `extra_2pct` outputs.
